evidence.snippet: This effect could be blocked by the selective β(1)-adrenergic receptor antagonist metoprolol, PKA inhibitor H89, and p38 MAPK inhibitor SB203580.

paper.title: β1-Adrenoceptor autoantibodies from DCM patients enhance the proliferation of T lymphocytes through the β1-AR/cAMP/PKA and p38 MAPK pathways.

evidence.snippet: prolonged treatment with of β(2) AR agonist, fenoterol, in combination with a β(1) AR blocker, metoprolol, is more effective than β(1) AR blocker alone
evidence.explanation: Metoprolol is a beta-1 adrenergic receptor blocker, decreasing receptor activity.

evidence.snippet: selective stimulation of β(1) AR activates the proapoptotic signaling pathways, while selective stimulation of β(2) AR is antiapoptotic
evidence.explanation: Activation of beta-1 adrenergic receptor triggers pro-apoptotic signaling pathways in cardiomyocytes.

paper.title: β₂ AR agonists in treatment of chronic heart failure: long path to translation.
paper.journal: Journal of molecular and cellular cardiology

evidence.snippet: PKA inhibition protected myocytes from death induced by β1-adrenergic receptor agonists by preventing cytosolic and sarcoplasmic reticulum Ca(2+) overload and calcium/calmodulin-dependent kinase II activation.
evidence.explanation: Beta-1 adrenergic receptor agonists drive myocyte death through PKA and CaMKII pathways.

paper.title: Cardiotoxic and cardioprotective features of chronic β-adrenergic signaling.

evidence.snippet: Loss of cardiomyocytes due to apoptosis is one mechanism that undoubtedly contributes to cardiac remodeling and functional deterioration associated with dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM).
evidence.explanation: Cardiomyocyte apoptosis contributes to progressive cardiac remodeling and functional deterioration seen in heart failure.

paper.title: β₂ AR agonists in treatment of chronic heart failure: long path to translation.
paper.journal: Journal of molecular and cellular cardiology

evidence.snippet: Selective beta(1)-blockade with high dose of metoprolol initiated in the early postinfarct phase improves myocardial energy metabolism and function and prevents overactivation of sympathetic system.
evidence.explanation: Metoprolol treatment improves cardiac function and energy metabolism in a heart failure model.

paper.title: Selective beta(1)-blockade improves cardiac bioenergetics and function and decreases neuroendocrine activation in rats during early postinfarct remodeling.

evidence.snippet: Several well designed, large scale randomized clinical trials including CIBS-II (bisoprolol), MERIT-HF (metoprolol succinate), and Copernicus (carvedilol) among others, have been conducted in patients with HFRef and demonstrated an improvement in cardiac mortality and morbidity.
evidence.explanation: Multiple large clinical trials demonstrate that metoprolol succinate improves cardiac mortality and morbidity in heart failure.

paper.title: The safety and tolerability of beta blockers in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction: is the current underutilization of this evidence-based therapy justified?
